newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Trinidad in talks on four oil exploration blocks.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad in talks on four oil exploration blocks.

text.p: Trinidad is in talks with three international consortiums to sign oil and gas exploration contracts in four offshore blocks, a government official said on Tuesday.

The government identified "preferred bidders" for just four of the nine blocks offered in the bidding round, when companies were chosen on the basis of planned exploration investment, said Rupert Mends, permanent secretary at the Ministry of Energy.
"They are the preferred bidders and they still have to negotiate the contract. We always give the companies an opportunity to negotiate the contract," he told Reuters by telephone.

A consortium of Anglo-Dutch Shell Exploration and Italy's Agip was chosen for block 25A, U.S. Exxon for blocks 25B and 26, and a consortium of U.S. Atlantic Richfield, Union Texas and Brazil's Petrobras for block 27.
All four blocks are located about 60 miles east of Trinidad in deep water.

While contract details still have to be decided, Trinidad's production-sharing contract allows the winning consortium to explore for oil and gas at its own cost, but then recoup the costs from any production revenue.
